```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(appusageR)
data(appusage_demo)
```

The package and dictionary have independent versions. This tutorial uses small
teaching dictionaries for the existing fictional apps. The bundled dictionary
is read as a dataset and remains unchanged.

```{r dictionary}
data(app_category_dictionary)
attr(app_category_dictionary, "dictionary_provenance")$dictionary_version
dictionary <- data.frame(
  App_UUID = c("org.example.reader", "org.example.music", "org.example.notes"),
  App_Name = c("Demo Reader", "Demo Music", "Demo Notes"),
  Level_1_Category = c("Education and Business", "Music and Audio", "Utilities and Tools"),
  Level_2_Category = c("Books and Reference", "Music Playback", "System Utilities"))
record <- appusage_demo$records$line_seven_days$data
classified <- add_app_categories(record, dictionary)
table(classified$daily$app_category_disposition)
stopifnot(identical(classified$daily$duration_ms, record$daily$duration_ms))
```

The public dictionary contains five character columns. Its `Others / Unclassified`
rows are provisional classifications; a dictionary match to that pair is not a
functional label or evidence of low usage. A runtime residual assigned by a
measured priority profile has a separate disposition.

## Resolve candidates within the package

Use two different label candidates for the same fictional Reader package, plus a
unique Music candidate. The extra names below are deliberate teaching aliases.

```{r conflicts}
conflicting <- rbind(dictionary[1:2, ], data.frame(
  App_UUID = "org.example.reader", App_Name = "Reader Utility Alias",
  Level_1_Category = "Utilities and Tools", Level_2_Category = "System Utilities"))
apps <- unique(record$daily[, c("package_name", "app_name")])
reader <- apps[apps$package_name == "org.example.reader", ]
music <- apps[apps$package_name == "org.example.music", ]
cases <- rbind(reader, reader, music)
cases$app_name <- c("Demo Reader", "Unlisted Reader Alias", "Demo Reader")
decisions <- add_app_categories(cases, conflicting)
decisions
stopifnot(decisions$app_category_match_method[1L] == "app_uuid_name",
          decisions$Level_2_Category[1L] == "Books and Reference",
          is.na(decisions$Level_1_Category[2L]),
          decisions$app_category_disposition[2L] == "needs_review_conflict",
          decisions$Level_2_Category[3L] == "Music Playback",
          isTRUE(decisions$app_category_name_disagreement[3L]))
```

The exact Reader name resolves the first row inside its APK candidates. The
unlisted alias leaves two different category pairs and remains pending. The Music
APK wins over a conflicting Reader name and records that disagreement. Duplicate
dictionary rows with identical L1/L2 labels agree; they are not category conflicts.
Conflicts never become automatic `Others / Unclassified`.

## Profile unknown apps with an explicit denominator

```{r profile}
known_reader <- dictionary[1L, ]
sources <- data.frame(source_id = "line_seven_days", person_id = "101",
  observation_id = "DEMO-001", selected_primary = TRUE)
profile <- profile_uncoded_apps(sources, known_reader,
  data = list(line_seven_days = record))
profile$apps[, c("app_key", "n_people_positive", "n_people_denominator",
                 "prevalence", "max_person_share", "disposition")]
music_profile <- profile$apps[profile$apps$package_name == "org.example.music", ]
stopifnot(music_profile$n_people_denominator == 1L,
          music_profile$n_people_positive == 1L, music_profile$prevalence == 1,
          abs(music_profile$max_person_share - 2/3) < 1e-12)
profiled <- add_app_categories(record, known_reader, profile = profile)
table(profiled$daily$app_category_disposition)
```

Music contributes 20 of the 30 recorded minutes per day. Its maximum primary-file
share is 2/3; it occurs with positive foreground use in 1 of 1 eligible people.
The default **share >= 5% OR prevalence >= 1%** rule puts it in priority review.
These are dictionary-maintenance thresholds. They do not change QC or sample
eligibility. Population prevalence counts people, not files, and repeated waves
contribute each person's maximum primary-file share. `extract_uncoded_apps()`
uses one duration source rather than adding event, episode and daily views.

If the same source is an alternate file rather than a selected primary, its
identity is retained but it cannot supply the primary-use denominator:

```{r insufficient}
alternate <- sources
alternate$selected_primary <- FALSE
pending <- profile_uncoded_apps(alternate, known_reader,
  data = list(line_seven_days = record))
pending$apps[, c("app_key", "n_people_denominator", "disposition")]
stopifnot(all(pending$apps$n_people_denominator == 0L))
```

Missing measurements and alternate-only identities are statistical insufficiency,
not measured zero use. Automatic residuals require adequate measurements below
both thresholds. In this one-person example every positively observed unknown app
has 100% prevalence, so no automatic residual is expected. To inspect a provisional
dictionary residual without changing the priority rule, use an explicit teaching
row:

```{r residual}
provisional <- dictionary[1:2, ]
provisional$Level_1_Category[2L] <- "Others"
provisional$Level_2_Category[2L] <- "Unclassified"
labels <- add_app_categories(record, provisional)$daily
is_residual <- labels$Level_1_Category == "Others" & labels$Level_2_Category == "Unclassified"
data.frame(measure = c("functional dictionary rows", "provisional dictionary rows"),
           n = c(sum(!is_residual), sum(is_residual)), denominator = nrow(labels))
stopifnot(sum(is_residual) == 7L, sum(!is_residual) == 7L)
```

Report functional matches, provisional/automatic residuals, priority review,
conflicts and insufficient statistics separately. Keep the denominator explicit:
the table above counts 14 daily rows, whereas the profile counts two app identities
and one person. Author-approved additions belong in a versioned dictionary; a
later update can replace residual labels.

## First-time classification and independent cache updates

Use both line and meta uploads to check that classification reaches every source.

```{r cache-paths}
folder <- system.file("extdata", "synth", package = "appusageR", mustWork = TRUE)
paths <- file.path(folder, appusage_demo$sources$source_relpath[1:2])
work <- tempfile("appusage-categories-")
plain_dir <- file.path(work, "plain")
fresh_dir <- file.path(work, "fresh")
plain_config <- appusage_config(execution = list(parallel = FALSE, workers = 1L, progress = FALSE))
plain <- run_appusage_workflow(paths, project_dir = plain_dir, config = plain_config)
read_data <- function(path) {
  env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  stopifnot(identical(load(path, envir = env), "data"))
  env$data
}
before <- lapply(plain$second_level$second_level_data_file, read_data)
qc_before <- lapply(plain$second_level$second_level_metadata_file,
  function(path) jsonlite::read_json(path, simplifyVector = FALSE)$qc)
updated <- write_app_categories_batch(plain_dir, dictionary, workers = 1L, progress = FALSE)
again <- write_app_categories_batch(plain_dir, dictionary, workers = 1L, progress = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(updated) == 2L, all(updated$action == "run"), all(again$action == "reuse"))
fresh_config <- appusage_config(category = list(enabled = TRUE, dictionary = dictionary),
  execution = list(parallel = FALSE, workers = 1L, progress = FALSE))
fresh <- run_appusage_workflow(paths, project_dir = fresh_dir, config = fresh_config)
for (i in seq_along(before)) {
  after <- read_data(plain$second_level$second_level_data_file[i])
  during <- read_data(fresh$second_level$second_level_data_file[i])
  for (grain in c("event", "episode", "daily")) {
    for (column in names(before[[i]][[grain]])) {
      stopifnot(identical(before[[i]][[grain]][[column]], after[[grain]][[column]]))
    }
    for (attribute in setdiff(names(attributes(before[[i]][[grain]])), "names")) {
      stopifnot(identical(attr(before[[i]][[grain]], attribute), attr(after[[grain]], attribute)))
    }
    stopifnot(identical(after[[grain]]$Level_1_Category, during[[grain]]$Level_1_Category),
              identical(after[[grain]]$Level_2_Category, during[[grain]]$Level_2_Category))
  }
  qc_after <- jsonlite::read_json(plain$second_level$second_level_metadata_file[i],
                                 simplifyVector = FALSE)$qc
  stopifnot(identical(qc_before[[i]], qc_after))
}
updated[, c("action", "status")]
```

The independent update uses existing paired proc-2 RDA/JSON files. Original
scientific columns and QC remain unchanged; a repeated identical category update
reuses the intact pair. For flat copied caches, supply an explicit RDA/JSON
manifest to `update_app_categories_cache()`. This updates annotations without
selecting questionnaire relationships.

```{r cleanup}
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
```
